chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from more than one, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who advanced dirhams for food, so the one who owed him was freed (from the debt of food), and he sent him the dirhams, saying: 'Buy food and fulfill your right.' He asked: 'Do you see any harm in that?' He replied: 'There will be someone else with him who will fulfill that for him.'

key_terms.أَسْلَفَ: Advanced (money/goods) as a loan or pre-payment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on advancing money for food and then receiving money back to buy food?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the validity of *salaf* (advance payment for goods) when the debtor converts the obligation into a monetary debt and returns the funds for the creditor to purchase the commodity themselves. The Imam’s ruling that 'there is no harm' provided the debtor fulfills the obligation highlights the flexibility in commercial contracts within Shia fiqh, distinguishing between the initial advance and the subsequent settlement mechanism. This hadith is pivotal in understanding the conditions under which deferred payment contracts remain valid without falling into riba (usury), emphasizing the role of mutual consent and fulfillment of the specific commodity's value.
